deities: Lord Narasimha (fourth avatar of Vishnu, half-man half-lion); the winter idol (Utsav Murti) of Lord Badrivishal is also worshipped here when Badrinath is closed

history.dynasty: Attributed to Adi Shankaracharya (8th century); idol installed during the reign of Lalitaditya Yukta Pida of Kashmir
history.period: ~8th century CE (about 1,200 years old per travel sources)
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the Narsingh (Narasimha Badri) Temple in Lower Bazaar, Joshimath, is the famous ~8th-century shrine established by Adi Shankaracharya, dedicated to Vishnu's Narasimha avatar. The small Shaligram-stone idol (~10 inches/25 cm, seated in lotus posture) is flanked by shrines/images of Badrivishal, Rama, Lakshmana, Sita, Garuda, Kubera, Uddhava and Chandika. It is the official winter seat of Badrinath - the Badrinath Utsav Murti is brought here for the six months Badrinath Dham lies under snow. It is counted among the Sapt Badri temples. The famous prophecy: the idol's arm/wrist (left or right, sources differ) is said to be thinning, and when it falls, the route to Badrinath will be blocked and worship will shift to Bhavishya Badri.

name: Narsingh Temple, Joshimath (Narasimha Badri)
town_description: Joshimath (Jyotirmath), in Chamoli district at ~1,890 m, is the first of Adi Shankaracharya's four maths and the winter seat of Badrinath. It is the gateway town for the Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib and Badrinath, and a base for Auli skiing. The Narsingh and Vasudev temples stand together in the lower part of the town.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, ~272 km (per chardhamyatratrip.com)
travel.road: In Lower Bazaar, Joshimath, on the Rishikesh-Badrinath route (NH 7/NH 58 corridor)

visitor_information.best_time: Open all year (unlike Badrinath); May-June and September-October are the busiest and most pleasant
